turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Welcome. Yeah, ready when you are.
What time did you go to bed last night?

Woke up in front of the TV, actually — must've dozed off around 2, 2:30 maybe. Got home from the evening shift about 11:30, figured I'd unwind a bit first, and that "a bit" turned into a couple hours.
Thanks for explaining that. Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night, and would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

Five hours, give or take — fell asleep around 2, up at 7. Wouldn't call it "well," more just adequate. Woke up stiff from the couch, but that's more a furniture problem than a sleep problem, if that makes sense.
That does make sense, thank you. What was the last activity you engaged in before properly falling asleep on the couch, and why did you choose to do that?
Last night I just had the TV on in the background — wasn't even watching anything in particular, just needed the noise to wind down after the shift.
Got it, thanks. What factors have most affected your sleep quality over the past two weeks?

Honestly, the shift changes are the biggest thing — I just came off a stretch of evenings, and when I'm on evenings I stay up too late unwinding and end up around five hours instead of six and a half. The traffic outside picks up early too, around six, so even if I wanted to sleep in it doesn't really happen. Fan helps drown some of that out, but it's mostly just the schedule bouncing around that throws things off.
Thanks, that’s clear. Is this pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently in terms of your schedule or sleep?

Pretty typical, yeah. It's been like this since I went on the rotating schedule — every time I flip to evenings, the same thing happens. I've kind of stopped expecting it to be any different at this point.
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?

Not really, no — it's not terrible, but "adequate" is about the ceiling of it. During evening weeks I'm running on five hours most nights, and I know that's not enough, I just haven't found a way around it that doesn't involve giving up my unwind time after a shift.
That makes sense. You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

Practical? Not really, no. On day-shift weeks maybe I'd get close, but during evening weeks getting even six is a stretch, let alone nine. It's a nice number on paper, but it doesn't really account for how shift work actually messes with your clock.
Thanks for explaining that. What makes it easy or difficult for you to actually get that much sleep, given your current schedule and routine?

Time is fine, being awake at 2am isn't - so getting to bed earlier is the hard part. If I come straight home and skip the TV wind-down I could probably get closer to seven, but after a shift I just want an hour to decompress before I even think about sleeping.
Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this, too? Why or why not?

Not much, honestly — after a shift I keep the phone away and just have the TV on for background noise while I wind down. Screen's not really the issue for me, it's more that I let the TV run too long before actually lying down.
Thanks for explaining that. Do you regularly use social media at other times of day, and if so, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?
Not really, no. I check it a couple times during the day, mostly on breaks — nothing before bed though, once the TV's on that's kind of it until I fall asleep.
Thanks, that’s helpful. Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots, like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar apps?
Yeah, I've messed around with one of them a bit — mostly for work stuff, like drafting an email or looking something up quick. Nothing to do with sleep or anything like that, just practical use.
Thanks, that’s helpful. When did you first start using AI chatbots, and how often would you say you use them these days?

A guy at work showed me maybe a year, year and a half ago — needed help writing up an inventory discrepancy report and he just typed it into one of these things. I use it maybe once a week now, if that, mostly quick stuff like that.
Thanks, that’s clear. Do you feel like your sleeping habits have changed at all since you began using social media or AI chatbots regularly?
Not really — sleep's more tied to whatever shift I'm on than anything I'm doing on a screen. If anything I use those apps less around bedtime, not more.
That’s helpful to know, thank you. If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?
Probably just being more disciplined about winding down instead of letting the TV drag on — going to bed at a set time instead of whenever the couch wins.
Given your work, studies, or daily responsibilities, do you think making that change—having a set bedtime and cutting the TV earlier—would be doable? Why or why not?

That mostly comes down to me, not the schedule — the shift work I can't control, but staying up with the TV is my own doing. Realistically though, some nights I'll still cave, especially coming off an evening shift when I'm wound up. I'd say doable, just not something I'll nail every night.
58, and I coordinate inventory at a warehouse. Born and still living in the same country — never moved, so that last one doesn't really apply to me.

Thanks for sharing that. We’ve covered all the main questions I had.

Before we wrap up, is there anything else about your sleep or your routine that you’d like to add that we haven’t talked about?
